objective: Use canonical-only LiveKit and Pipecat EOS parameters in the UI and backend, with a one-time reversible migration of stored audio options.
verified_context: EOS provider selection is microphone.eos.provider in assistant_deployment_audio_options, not assistant_deployment_audios.audio_provider.
Audio options have unique (key, assistant_deployment_audio_id) pairs and application-generated positive IDs, not SQL-generated IDs.
Migration 000060 removed created_by and updated_by. Current option rows have created_actor_type/id and updated_actor_type/id.
The provider JSON files already expose canonical controls. UI hydration and LiveKit/Pipecat constructors still translate legacy keys.
Current UI scoped replacement can discard backend-only EOS model paths. Canonical-only hydration must preserve these explicit overrides.
Silence-based EOS uses microphone.eos.timeout as its canonical key and must not be changed.

cmd/assistant/assistant.go logs migration failures without preventing startup and can force-clear dirty state. This migration must be applied and verified externally before canonical-only code is deployed.
bin/verify-phase3-migrations.sh runs full migration history and hard-codes assistant-api version 60. It needs a minimal update to 61.
Local migrate, psql, postgres, initdb and pg_ctl are available for disposable database tests.
Prior model-quality and model-asset concerns remain unresolved and are not addressed by a parameter migration.

parameter_contract.missing_values: Do not insert new option rows or persist duplicated defaults. Existing canonical backend/UI defaults supply absent values.
parameter_contract.manual_selection: Preserve EOS provider and existing nonblank LiveKit model values, including custom model names. Never infer a model from language.

migration.target: All input-audio deployment rows whose stored EOS provider exactly equals livekit_eos or pipecat_smart_turn_eos. Include inactive target records so later activation does not restore old keys. Do not guess missing/unknown providers.
algorithm: Run atomically with bounded lock and statement timeouts; block concurrent option/deployment writes while reading, journaling and updating the target set.

Validate candidate values before any changes. Presence precedence is canonical first, then the listed aliases; do not silently reset or choose a lower-priority value when a present candidate is invalid.

Accept finite decimal/exponent numeric text with Go-compatible digit separators and no outer whitespace. Report and abort on non-finite, malformed, hex-float or out-of-range input requiring manual review. Do not silently coerce it with PostgreSQL's broader parser.

Preserve zero and custom finite numeric values; do not add tuning bounds that differ from existing runtime behavior. Preserve positive integer max_history_turns and nonblank model values; report unsupported history/model values for manual review.

When canonical exists and is valid, preserve its row/value. Otherwise rename the highest-priority existing valid alias row in place, preserving its ID and audit fields. Remove lower-priority aliases and known obsolete keys only after choosing the canonical survivor.
Keep unknown EOS keys, unrelated metadata, non-target providers, output audio, provider rows and backend model path overrides unchanged.

Store original and resulting row images for only changed/deleted rows in a migration-specific journal, plus the target provider/deployment identity needed to guard rollback. Do not invent application IDs or user audit identities.
Repeat application must not overwrite the journal's original images, resurrect aliases or modify already migrated values. A no-change run is a no-op.
rollback: Run under the same transaction and write exclusion as up.
Compare affected rows and provider identity with journaled post-migration state before changing anything. Also detect destination key/ID conflicts and missing/deleted parent deployments.
If any affected row was subsequently edited or any identity conflicts, abort the entire rollback and retain the journal. Never silently skip conflicts and report complete rollback.
Otherwise restore original row IDs, keys, values, status and audit fields exactly, then remove the migration journal in the successful transaction.
migration.rollout: Ship migration files first to an operator-controlled migration job. Stop configuration writes/old application instances, run preflight and migration successfully, verify version 61 clean and target alias count zero, then deploy canonical-only backend/UI. Startup's warning-only migration behavior is not an approval or rollout gate.
migration.live_execution: Not authorized by this task. No shared database is contacted or changed; later environment selection and rollout approval are separate.

ui_backend_changes: Remove alias arrays, float-spelling parsing and legacy fallback preservation from GetDefaultEOSConfig. Use the existing provider config/default APIs for canonical keys.
Retain backend-only EOS model paths through EOS hydration and the calling STT configuration flow; preserve unrelated metadata and caller-owned input arrays.

Update the provider-switch handler in configure-audio-input.tsx so its broad EOS-prefix filter retains backend-only model paths before canonical hydration. Do not restore old provider-specific control values on a provider switch.

Preserve existing canonical defaults, valid zero values, custom thresholds, timeout values and manual LiveKit model/history selections. Remove known stale provider-specific controls when switching providers.
Delete LiveKit/Pipecat constructor alias reads and private alias constants. Keep canonical keys and defaults unchanged.
Remove the global legacy silence_timeout constant only if no remaining references need it. Keep MicrophoneEOSOptionTimeout for silence-based EOS.
Update existing canonical/legacy parity tests to prove legacy keys no longer configure LiveKit or Pipecat and that migration is the only translation path.

ownership.rfcs/0016-eos-canonical-parameters.md: coordinator (bounded challenge correction after RFC author completion)

principles.kiss: Rename existing rows once and remove runtime alias branches; do not generate IDs or persist duplicated defaults.
principles.yagni: No permanent alias framework, compatibility flag or model-selection automation.
principles.single_source_of_truth: Retain canonical provider definitions and runtime defaults; a migration journal is recovery evidence, not live configuration.
principles.contracts: Preserve canonical parameter spelling, valid values, manual model selection and packet/API behavior. Legacy reads end after verified migration.
principles.fail_safe: Preflight and rollback conflicts abort atomically. Migration failure blocks rollout, regardless of startup behavior.
principles.security: Only target EOS rows; retain audit identity without inventing actors. Report IDs/keys/counts, not option contents, credentials or audio.
principles.observability: Record migration counts, clean schema version, obsolete-key counts and rollback conflicts in operator verification evidence.
principles.reversibility: Journal exact before/after images and restore only when post-state and provider identity still match.

non_goals: No dispatch, VAD, STT transport, telephony, schema-contract or API changes beyond the migration journal
No model-asset migration or model-quality claim
No blanket reset of custom settings
No new helpers/utils or permanent compatibility layer
No commit/push/merge of application changes before required review
risks: Configuration writers must be stopped during migration and rollback
Malformed or non-decimal values block migration for explicit operator review
Backend aliases cannot be removed before migration verification
Rollback after user edits intentionally fails instead of erasing edits
Full-table write exclusion needs a bounded maintenance window; size and timing require the later environment's dry-run inventory
required_commands: just agent-finalize "$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRT HEAD | paste -sd, -),$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard | paste -sd, -)"
acceptance_criteria: UI/backend contain no active LiveKit/Pipecat alias read paths; silence-based behavior is unchanged.
Migration preserves existing canonical values, manual models, custom finite values, zero, backend paths, other providers and unrelated metadata.

Migration tests cover both providers, every alias priority, conflicts, missing values, inactive records, output audio, invalid/non-finite/hex values, separators, overflow, transaction rollback and repeated execution.
Down restores original rows exactly and rejects later edits/provider switches/unique conflicts atomically without dropping its journal.
UI tests cover canonical happy paths, ignored legacy values, model-path preservation, provider switching and input ownership.
Backend tests cover canonical success, default/error paths and ignored legacy aliases using real constructors.
Full migration history reaches clean version 61 and the focused disposable PostgreSQL suite passes.
No live database was used, no model-quality approval is implied, and detached checkout is preserved.
